sonnet.problem: The question asks the baker to supply the exact opening line of Psalm 124 ('If the LORD had not been on our side'). The story card before it only says David 'opens with a big what-if' and gives no content for the baker to reason from. The baker is left guessing the wording of a line, and the wrong answers (walls, king) are equally plausible, so a right pick is luck.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line. / Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. / The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
